description: A 35% debt-to-income ratio passes most US lenders. Gulf banks cap installments at 50% of salary in the UAE, 33.33% in Saudi Arabia and 40% in Kuwait. Web page: https://calcbright.com/debt-to-income-calculator

cardLimit.description: Total credit card limits Optional. Many UAE banks count 5% of every card limit, used or not, instead of the minimum payment.

earner.description: Income from Retirees have a lower cap: 30% of the pension in the UAE and Kuwait, 25% in Saudi Arabia.

housing.description: Monthly rent Gulf banks leave rent out of the debt burden ratio; US lenders count it, or the new mortgage payment with tax and insurance.

income.description: Gross monthly income Before tax and deductions – in Kuwait, salary after deductions.

other.description: Other debt payments Overdraft and buy-now-pay-later installments, child support, alimony.

rules.description: Lender rules Gulf central banks cap the share of salary that loan installments may take; US lenders use guideline ratios.
